Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning · Computing & programming

comment noun and verb

a written note on a text

also annotation, annotate, comments on a draft, leave a comment, code comment, notes in the margin

classical

Plin. Ep. 7.20.2: librum meum cum adnotātiōnibus tuīs exspectō
Gell. praef. (Lewis & Short)

adnotātiō, adnotātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a written comment, a note on a text

Lewis & Short, under annotātiō, which it would rather spell adn-: “a noting down in writing, a remark, annotation (post-Aug.)”.

Other words

  • adnotō, adnotāre, adnotāvī, adnotātum — comment on, mark (points in a text)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 7.20.1: adnotāvī quae commūtanda, quae eximenda arbitrārer

    What Pliny and Tacitus did with each other’s books, and what a reviewer does to a draft or to code. Post-Augustan, like the noun.

Examples

  • Librum tuum lēgī et, quam dīligentissimē potuī, adnotāvī quae commūtanda, quae eximenda arbitrārer. … Nunc ā tē librum meum cum adnotātiōnibus tuīs exspectō.

    I’ve read your book and, as carefully as I could, marked what I thought should be changed and what cut. … Now I’m waiting for my own book back from you, with your comments.Plin. Ep. 7.20.1–2

See also comment, code review.

SourcesLewis & Short: annotatio · Lewis & Short: annoto
